doc.title: Fred Radke interviewed by Monk Rowe, Hillsdale, Michigan, November 8, 2023

title: Subbing lead trumpet at the Fairmont Hotel show at 16
summary: Contractor Jack Fisher hired the 16-year-old for a show and dance, and he played lead when the regular player arrived late.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: so I get the experience to say that I’ve played a show so I can get other jobs to play shows and dances.” And it’s silence. And Jack Fisher says, “Be there at 7:00.” So now I show up there, right? And I get there early and we’re in the room and there’s like twelve musicians and typical talk-over. “Okay we’ve got a dog act, a singer, juggler” whatever the heck it was. And they said, “Okay the first thing is now we vamp at Letter A, we vamp ‘til the act enters the thing and then when they throw the ball up in the air we play this chord and then we — da-da-da — and everybody’s got their pencil out. I’m standing there and I had the first trumpet book because the other trumpet player isn’t there. And I said, “Who’s playing lead?” And they said so and so — Merv Gruthers or somebody. And he says, “Well where is he?” And he says, “I don’t know where he is, you take the book.” So I’m watching everybody, how they’re marking — and watching the little thing, used to put glasses

Remember drawing glasses to say “Look out here!” And so I’m watching these guys. So now it gets like 15 minutes before the show and in walks the trumpet player. “God I’m sorry, I was caught in traffic.” And Fisher says, “I don’t care, that’s not an excuse. As you know professional musicians, you’re dead if you’re late. Never be tardy, ever. And so he says, “Well I’m sorry, where’s my music?” And he says, “Here.” He said, “Well this is the second trumpet book.” And he said, “That’s right, that’s what you’re playing. Fred’s playing lead.” “Who the hell are you?” I said, “I’m Fred Radke.” And he says, “Yeah? What do you do?” I said, “Well obviously I’m going to play the trumpet.” And he says, “You’re playing lead and I’m playing second? Well you better be real good.” So like Bobby Shew said in that interview, “Do you know this guy Bobby Shew?” “Yeah.” “He plays all the high notes, man he never misses. Have you heard his jazz playing?” “Oh yeah, he’s great, he’s something else.” But he says, “Go out to a gig and miss one F then they say, “You know this guy Bobby Shew, you know he missed an F?” And they said, “Oh yeah, I know.” Well it’s the same thing. That was the proving ground that night for me.
Perfect. I played — really, playing a dog act and playing some chords. You know play “Saints Go Marching In” or something.
